title: How many units are there in Step 10 and Step y?
description: Two patterns of units are read from their first three steps. For each one the next figure and Step ten are found, and an expression is written for Step y, then tested with the first three steps.
teaching_notes: One idea: see each step as a square plus extras, write it with the step number, and test it with the steps given. Watch for students who add the same number to each step instead of squaring.

source: Figure it Out (identities and patterns, question 11)
video_script.why: The child has written an expression for the circles pattern with the step number, and now does the same for two new patterns of units.
video_script.substitution: Read each step as a square, write it with the step number y, find the next figure and Step ten, and test with the first three steps.
video_script.anchor: two patterns of units, each shown by its first three steps
video_script.payoff_line: The first pattern has y plus two, all squared, and Step ten has one hundred forty four units

final_answer.spoken: the first pattern has y plus two, all squared, and Step ten has one hundred forty four units; the second has y plus one, all squared, plus y, and Step ten has one hundred thirty one

maths_rules: (a) Steps 1 to 3 have 9, 16, 25 units: 3², 4², 5²; side = step + 2; Step y has (y + 2)²
(b) Steps 1 to 3 have 5, 11, 19 units: 2² + 1, 3² + 2, 4² + 3; Step y has (y + 1)² + y
video_script.design: One idea: read each step as a square, then write it with the step number. The two patterns stay in the anchor band; the numbers sit on the working board.

beats.on_screen: a small title card From your book; pattern (a) with Steps 1 to 3 of 9, 16 and 25 units; pattern (b) with Steps 1 to 3 of 5, 11 and 19 units

marks.book: the small title card From your book appears
marks.pats: pattern (a) and pattern (b) appear, each with three steps
marks.nums: the counts 9, 16, 25 and 5, 11, 19 appear under the steps
marks.ask: the words next figure, Step 10, Step y appear

narration: <bookmark mark='book'/>This question is from your book.
<bookmark mark='pats'/>It shows two patterns, each with three steps.
<bookmark mark='nums'/>The first has nine, sixteen and twenty five units. The second has five, eleven and nineteen.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>Draw the next figure, find the units in Step ten, and write an expression for Step y.

beats.on_screen: the two patterns hold still and the words Step y glow

marks.stop: the words Step y glow in the accent colour

narration: <bookmark mark='stop'/>Think and tell.

beats.on_screen: the circles pattern: Step k has k² + 2k circles; Step 4: 4² + 2 × 4 = 24

marks.see: Step k has k² + 2k circles appears
marks.test: k = 4 is put in and 4² + 2 × 4 = 24 appears

narration: <bookmark mark='see'/>In the circles pattern, we wrote the number of circles using the step number.
<bookmark mark='test'/>Then we put in a step number to find the circles at that step.

beats.on_screen: Given: (a) 9, 16, 25 units; (b) 5, 11, 19 units in Steps 1 to 3

marks.given: the counts of both patterns are written on the board

narration: <bookmark mark='given'/>Given, the units in the first three steps of each pattern.

beats.on_screen: To find: the next figure, the units in Step 10, and the units in Step y, for (a) and (b)

marks.find: the three things to find are written

narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to find the next figure, Step ten, and Step y for each pattern.
<bookmark mark='nums'/>First, look at the first pattern. Nine is three squared, sixteen is four squared, and twenty five is five squared.
<bookmark mark='rule'/>The side is the step number plus two, so Step y has y plus two, all squared.

beats.on_screen: (a) next figure, Step 4: side 6, 6² = 36; Step 10: side 12, 12² = 144

marks.next: the next figure, a square of side 6, is drawn and 6² = 36 is written

beats.colours: the new figure in the accent colour
narration: <bookmark mark='next'/>Second, draw the next figure. Step four is a square of side six, with thirty six units.
<bookmark mark='ten'/>For Step ten, the side is twelve. Twelve squared is one hundred forty four.

marks.rule: square of step + 1, plus the step number, and (y + 1)² + y are written

beats.colours: the squares and the extra units in two colours
narration: <bookmark mark='nums'/>Third, look at the second pattern. Five is two squared plus one, and eleven is three squared plus two.
Nineteen is four squared plus three.
<bookmark mark='rule'/>The square has side step plus one, and the extra units equal the step number. Step y has y plus one, all squared, plus y.

marks.next: the next figure is drawn and 5² + 4 = 29 is written

beats.colours: the new figure in the accent colour
narration: <bookmark mark='next'/>Fourth, draw the next figure. Step four is five squared plus four, which is twenty nine.
<bookmark mark='ten'/>Step ten is eleven squared plus ten. That is one hundred twenty one plus ten, which is one hundred thirty one.

marks.back: the words put the answers back in the question are written
marks.first: y = 1, 2, 3 give 9, 16 and 25 for the first pattern, each ticked
marks.second: y = 1 gives 2² + 1 = 5 and y = 2 gives 3² + 2 = 11, each ticked

narration: <bookmark mark='back'/>Fifth, put the answers back in the question.
<bookmark mark='first'/>In the first pattern, y as one, two and three give three squared, four squared and five squared. These are nine, sixteen and twenty five.
<bookmark mark='second'/>In the second pattern, y as one gives four plus one, which is five. Y as two gives nine plus two, which is eleven.
<bookmark mark='third'/>Y as three gives sixteen plus three, which is nineteen.

beats.on_screen: Answer: (a) (y + 2)², Step 10 has 144 (b) (y + 1)² + y, Step 10 has 131

marks.ans: the answer for the first pattern is boxed
marks.two: the answer for the second pattern is boxed

narration: <bookmark mark='ans'/>The first pattern has y plus two, all squared, and Step ten has one hundred forty four units.
<bookmark mark='two'/>The second has y plus one, all squared, plus y, and Step ten has one hundred thirty one.
